Convert your PDF

PDF to Markdown With MarkItDown

Install Microsoft MarkItDown with the PDF extra, then run markitdown input.pdf -o output.md. Before using that Markdown for AI search, check one key phrase per page and make sure table values stayed with the right rows. If a page is only an image, run optical character recognition (OCR) on that page and verify its text before indexing it.

  1. Convert a local PDF
  2. Decide what to check next
  3. Check rows and reading order
  4. Recover text from a scan
  5. Prepare the result for AI search
  6. See the actual outputs

Convert a PDF locally

Use Python in an isolated environment. The commands below use a POSIX shell on macOS or Linux. The last command writes the Markdown to a new file. Choose an unused filename if you already have edited Markdown in that folder.

python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install 'markitdown[pdf]==0.1.9'
markitdown input.pdf -o output.md

For the same inputs we tested, download the three-page support-notes PDF. Replace input.pdf with support-notes.pdf. The example uses the local converter without optional OCR or cloud extraction plugins.

Check table rows and reading order

Pick a cell where a wrong association would change the answer. On page 2 of our fixture, 45 days belongs to Extended, and 14 days belongs to Standard. Compare whole rows in the Markdown with the PDF, including headers and footnotes. If the source has two columns, check that the output reads each column in the expected order.

For a row that gets split or detached from its heading, fix the row or keep the original page reference before loading it into an AI search system.

Recover text from an image-only page

Try selecting text on the page in a PDF viewer. If the page is an image, apply OCR to a copy of that page. With Poppler and Swift installed on macOS, download the local English OCR script, then run:

pdftoppm -f 3 -l 3 -r 150 -png support-notes.pdf support-page
swift ocr-page.swift support-page-3.png > page-3-ocr.txt

Set both page arguments to the actual page number you are checking and use the PNG filename produced by Poppler. Compare the recognized characters with the source, especially IDs, units and deadlines. This script uses Apple Vision with English recognition. A source in another language needs OCR configured for that language.

Keep the source page with the text you index

  1. Verify one fact from each page and one important row from each table. If you are unsure a page has a text layer, check a visible phrase against the Markdown.
  2. Keep the original PDF and a separate verified copy of the extracted text. Label any corrected scan text with its source file and page, then include it in the verified copy.
  3. After importing it into your AI search or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system, ask a question whose correct answer depends on the recovered text. For this fixture, ask how soon to escalate SCAN-43. Check for 72 hours from page 3.

What survived in the actual conversion

In our local MarkItDown 0.1.9 test, the Markdown retained the page 1 ticket ID and both table rows from page 2. It omitted the image-only exception on page 3. Apple Vision OCR on a raster copy of page 3 recovered SCAN-43 and 72 hours. We compared those values with the PDF.

Original PDF · Unedited MarkItDown output · Separate OCR output

Both conversions ran with external network access denied after dependency installation. We checked the extracted text and rows. Search or retrieval quality depends on the import and was outside this fixture test.

Official sources checked November 28, 2026. See Microsoft’s MarkItDown documentation and the MarkItDown project review (Chinese) for other formats. The test covers one synthetic PDF and one local OCR result.
